trs.20: I swear by the Day of Resurrection
trs.85: By the Day of Resurrection
trs.22: I do call to witness the Resurrection Day;
trs.203: I swear by the Day of Resurrection.

trs.20: And I swear by the reproaching soul<sup foot_note=197655>1</sup> [to the certainty of resurrection].
trs.85: and by the self-reproaching soul!
trs.22: And I do call to witness the self-reproaching spirit: (Eschew Evil).
trs.203: And I swear by the self-reproaching person (a believer).

trs.20: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?
trs.85: Does man think We shall not put his bones back together?
trs.22: Does man think that We cannot assemble his bones?
trs.203: Does man (a disbeliever) think that We shall not assemble his bones?

verses.text_uthmani: بَلَىٰ قَـٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُۥ

trs.20: Yes. [We are] Able [even] to proportion his fingertips.
trs.85: In fact, We can reshape his very fingertips.
trs.22: Nay, We are able to put together in perfect order the very tips of his fingers.
trs.203: Yes, We are Able to put together in perfect order the tips of his fingers.<sup foot_note=155022>1</sup>

trs.20: But man desires to continue in sin.<sup foot_note=197656>1</sup>
trs.85: Yet man wants to deny what is ahead of him:
trs.22: But man wishes to do wrong (even) in the time in front of him.
trs.203: Nay! Man (denies Resurrection and Reckoning. So he) desires to continue committing sins.

trs.20: He asks, "When is the Day of Resurrection?"
trs.85: he says, ‘So, when will this Day of Resurrection be?’
trs.22: He questions: "When is the Day of Resurrection?"
trs.203: He asks: "When will be this Day of Resurrection?"

trs.20: So when vision is dazzled.
trs.85: When eyes are dazzled
trs.22: At length, when the sight is dazed,
trs.203: So, when the sight shall be dazed.

trs.20: And the moon darkens.
trs.85: and the moon eclipsed,
trs.22: And the moon is buried in darkness.
trs.203: And the moon will be eclipsed.

trs.20: And the sun and the moon are joined,
trs.85: when the sun and the moon are brought together,
trs.22: And the sun and moon are joined together,-
trs.203: And the sun and moon will be joined together (by going one into the other or folded up or deprived of their light).<sup foot_note=155023>1</sup>

trs.20: Man will say on that Day, "Where is the [place of] escape?"
trs.85: on that Day man will say, ‘Where can I escape?’
trs.22: That Day will Man say: "Where is the refuge?"
trs.203: On that Day man will say: "Where (is the refuge) to flee?"

trs.20: No! There is no refuge.
trs.85: Truly, there is no refuge:
trs.22: By no means! No place of safety!
trs.203: No! There is no refuge!

trs.20: To your Lord, that Day, is the [place of] permanence.
trs.85: they will all return to your Lord on that Day.
trs.22: Before thy Lord (alone), that Day will be the place of rest.
trs.203: Unto your Lord (Alone) will be the place of rest that Day.

verses.text_uthmani: يُنَبَّؤُا۟ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ يَوْمَئِذٍۭ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ

trs.20: Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead<sup foot_note=197658>1</sup> and kept back.<sup foot_note=197657>2</sup>
trs.85: On that Day, man will be told what he put first and what he put last.
trs.22: That Day will Man be told (all) that he put forward, and all that he put back.
trs.203: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forward (of his evil good deeds), and what he left behind (of his good or evil traditions).

trs.20: Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,<sup foot_note=197659>1</sup>
trs.85: Truly, man is a clear witness against himself,
trs.22: Nay, man will be evidence against himself,
trs.203: Nay! Man will be a witness against himself [as his body parts (skin, hands, legs, etc.) will speak about his deeds],

trs.20: Even if he presents his excuses.
trs.85: despite all the excuses he may put forward.
trs.22: Even though he were to put up his excuses.
trs.203: Though he may put forth his excuses (to cover his evil deeds).

verses.text_uthmani: لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِۦٓ

trs.20: Move not your tongue with it, [O Muḥammad], to hasten with it [i.e., recitation of the Qur’ān].
trs.85: [Prophet], do not rush your tongue in an attempt to hasten [your memorization of] the Revelation:
trs.22: Move not thy tongue concerning the (Qur'an) to make haste therewith.
trs.203: Move not your tongue concerning (the Qur’ân, O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) to make haste therewith.

trs.20: Indeed, upon Us is its collection [in your heart] and [to make possible] its recitation.
trs.85: We shall make sure of its safe collection and recitation.
trs.22: It is for Us to collect it and to promulgate it:
trs.203: It is for Us to collect it and to give you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) the ability to recite it (the Qur’ân).

trs.20: So when We have recited it [through Gabriel], then follow its recitation.
trs.85: When We have recited it, repeat the recitation
trs.22: But when We have promulgated it, follow thou its recital (as promulgated):
trs.203: And when We have recited it to you [O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم through Jibrîl (Gabriel)], then follow its (the Qur’an’s) recital.

trs.20: Then upon Us is its clarification [to you].
trs.85: and We shall make it clear.
trs.22: Nay more, it is for Us to explain it (and make it clear):
trs.203: Then it is for Us (Allâh) to make it clear (to you).

trs.20: No! But you [i.e., mankind] love the immediate
trs.85: Truly you [people] love this fleeting world
trs.22: Nay, (ye men!) but ye love the fleeting life,
trs.203: Not [as you think, that you (mankind) will not be resurrected and recompensed for your deeds], but you (men) love the present life of this world,

trs.20: And leave [i.e., neglect] the Hereafter.
trs.85: and neglect the life to come.
trs.22: And leave alone the Hereafter.
trs.203: And neglect the Hereafter.

trs.20: [Some] faces, that Day, will be radiant,
trs.85: On that Day there will be radiant faces,
trs.22: Some faces, that Day, will beam (in brightness and beauty);-
trs.203: Some faces that Day shall be Nâdirah (shining and radiant).

trs.20: Looking at their Lord.<sup foot_note=197660>1</sup>
trs.85: looking towards their Lord,
trs.22: Looking towards their Lord;
trs.203: Looking at their Lord (Allâh).

trs.20: And [some] faces, that Day, will be contorted,
trs.85: and on that Day there will be the sad and despairing faces
trs.22: And some faces, that Day, will be sad and dismal,
trs.203: And some faces, that Day, will be Bâsirah (dark, gloomy, frowning, and sad),

trs.20: Expecting that there will be done to them [something] backbreaking.
trs.85: of those who realize that a great calamity is about to befall them.
trs.22: In the thought that some back-breaking calamity was about to be inflicted on them;
trs.203: Thinking that some calamity is about to fall on them.

trs.20: No! When it [i.e., the soul] has reached the collar bones<sup foot_note=197661>1</sup>
trs.85: Truly, when the soul reaches the collarbone;
trs.22: Yea, when (the soul) reaches to the collar-bone (in its exit),
trs.203: Nay, when (the soul) reaches to the collar bone (i.e. up to the throat in its exit),

trs.20: And it is said, "Who will cure [him]?"
trs.85: when it is said, ‘Could any charm-healer save him now?’;
trs.22: And there will be a cry, "Who is a magician (to restore him)?"
trs.203: And it will be said: "Who can cure him (and save him from death)?"

trs.20: And he [i.e., the dying one] is certain that it is the [time of] separation
trs.85: when he knows it is the final parting;
trs.22: And he will conclude that it was (the Time) of Parting;
trs.203: And he (the dying person) will conclude that it was (the time) of parting (death);

trs.20: And the leg is wound about the leg,<sup foot_note=197662>1</sup>
trs.85: when his legs are brought together:
trs.22: And one leg will be joined with another:
trs.203: And one leg will be joined with another leg (shrouded).<sup foot_note=155024>1</sup>

trs.20: To your Lord, that Day, will be the procession.<sup foot_note=197663>1</sup>
trs.85: on that day he will be driven towards your Lord.
trs.22: That Day the Drive will be (all) to thy Lord!
trs.203: The drive will be, on that Day, to your Lord (Allâh)!

trs.20: And he [i.e., the disbeliever] had not believed, nor had he prayed.
trs.85: He neither believed nor prayed,
trs.22: So he gave nothing in charity, nor did he pray!-
trs.203: So he (the disbeliever) neither believed (in this Qur’ân and in the Message of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) nor prayed!

trs.20: But [instead], he denied and turned away.
trs.85: but denied the truth and turned away,
trs.22: But on the contrary, he rejected Truth and turned away!
trs.203: But on the contrary, he belied (this Qur’ân and the Message of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) and turned away!

trs.20: And then he went to his people, swaggering [in pride].
trs.85: walking back to his people with a conceited swagger.
trs.22: Then did he stalk to his family in full conceit!
trs.203: Then he walked in conceit (full pride) to his family admiring himself!

trs.20: Woe to you, and woe!
trs.85: Closer and closer it comes to you.
trs.22: Woe to thee, (O men!), yea, woe!
trs.203: Woe to you [O man (disbeliever)]! And then (again) woe to you!

trs.20: Then woe to you, and woe!
trs.85: Closer and closer still.
trs.22: Again, Woe to thee, (O men!), yea, woe!
trs.203: Again, woe to you [O man (disbeliever)]! And then (again) woe to you!

trs.20: Does man think that he will be left neglected?<sup foot_note=197664>1</sup>
trs.85: Does man think he will be left alone?
trs.22: Does man think that he will be left uncontrolled, (without purpose)?
trs.203: Does man think that he will be left neglected (without being punished or rewarded for the obligatory duties enjoined by his Lord Allâh on him)?

verses.text_uthmani: أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِّن مَّنِىٍّ يُمْنَىٰ

trs.20: Had he not been a sperm from semen emitted?
trs.85: Was he not just a drop of spilt-out sperm,
trs.22: Was he not a drop of sperm emitted (in lowly form)?
trs.203: Was he not a Nutfah (mixed male and female sexual discharge) of semen emitted (poured forth)?

trs.20: Then he was a clinging clot, and [Allāh] created [his form] and proportioned [him]
trs.85: which became a clinging form, which God shaped in due proportion,
trs.22: Then did he become a leech-like clot; then did (Allah) make and fashion (him) in due proportion.
trs.203: Then he became an ‘Alaqah (a clot); then (Allâh) shaped and fashioned (him) in due proportion.<sup foot_note=155025>1</sup>

trs.20: And made of him two mates, the male and the female.
trs.85: fashioning from it the two sexes, male and female?
trs.22: And of him He made two sexes, male and female.
trs.203: And made of him two sexes, male and female.

verses.text_uthmani: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَـٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحْـِۧىَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ

trs.20: Is not that [Creator] Able to give life to the dead?
trs.85: Does He who can do this not have the power to bring the dead back to life?
trs.22: Has not He, (the same), the power to give life to the dead?
trs.203: Is not He (Allâh Who does that) Able to give life to the dead? (Yes! He is Able to do all things).
